This Appeal Coming On For Final Hearing This
Day, Judgment Was Delivered Therein As Under:
Coram: Hon'Ble Mrs. Justice P Sree Sudha
 Oral Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant/claimant under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 challenging the judgment and award dated 12.11.2024 passed in MVC No. 614/2021 on the file of the Additional Senior Civil Judge and Mact, Pandavapura, for enhancing the compensation.
2.
Heard the arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant and respondent.
The ranks of the parties are retained as per tribunal for the sake of convenience.
3. Injured/claimant met with an accident on 22.05.2021 and filed claim petition claiming compensation NC: 2026:KHC:6910 HC-KAR of Rs.17,00,000/-.
Tribunal considering the entire evidence on record granted an amount of Rs.5,71,723/- with interest and the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.

Aggrieved by the said award this appeal is preferred in which it is mainly contended that petitioner examined doctor and he assessed the disability as 40%, to the right lower limb, but the tribunal has taken only 12%.
He was working as a harvesting mason and also doing dairy farming and earning Rs. 25,000/- per month.
But the tribunal has taken his income as Rs.11,473/- and the amount granted under other heads is meager and thus requested for enhancement of the compensation.
4. Though petitioner stated that he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month, he has not filed any income proof.

As he met with an accident in the year 2021, his notional income is to be taken as Rs.15,000/-
per month as per the chart prepared by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.
He is aged 20 years and the multiplier taken is NC: 2026:KHC:6910 HC-KAR 18.

Petitioner sustained following injuries as per Ex.P2 wound certificate:

sentences.text: (1) Lacerated wound on the right leg middle 1/3 both bone fracture, and (2) Abrasion over the right forearm measuring 3 x 4 cm red in colour.
Injury No.1 is grievous and the injury No.2 is simple in nature.

5. Petitioner also examined PW2 and he stated that claimant suffered lacerated wounds on the right leg and when X-ray was done, it was found that Right leg middle 1/3 Both bone # fractured and hence, surgery was done on 23.05.2021 by CRIF with Tibia nailing and discharged him on 29.05.2021.

P.W.2 found that there is a decrease in movement of right knee by 40% and the muscles are weak by Grade-2 and movement of right ankle is decreased by 40% and muscles are weak by Grade-2 and that, the claimant has to spend approximately Rs.40,000/- to 45,000/- for removal of implants and that, the claimant is suffering from disability to an extent of 36%.
NC: 2026:KHC:6910 HC-KAR 6.

As petitioner met with an accident in the year 2021, his notional income was taken as Rs.15,000/-
per month and he is aged 20 years and the multiplier is 18.
The Tribunal Considered one third of 36% as 12% disability, and this Court finds no reason to interfere with the disability assessed by the doctor.
Therefore the loss of future earning capacity comes to Rs.3,88,800/- (15,000x12x18x12%).
Tribunal granted Rs.99,871/- towards medical expenses as per the bills filed before the Tribunal and it is confirmed.

7. Considering the nature of injuries, period of hospitalisation, his occupation and other relevant factors, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.50,000/- for pain and suffering,
Rs.30,000/- for loss of amenities, and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
Petitioner might not have attended any other work at least for a period of 3 months, therefore Rs.45,000/- is granted under the head loss of income during laid up period.
The Tribunal also NC: 2026:KHC:6910 HC-KAR granted Rs.45,000/- towards future medical expenses and it is confirmed.

Thus, the total compensation comes to Rs.6,88,671/-.
8.
In all, the claimant is entitled for the compensation of Rs.6,88,671/- with interest at 6% per annum as against Rs.5,71,723/- awarded by the Tribunal.

9. The award of compensation passed by the Tribunal is modified as under:
 Heads Amount in Rs.
 1. Loss of future income 3,88,800/-
 2. Medical expenses 99,871/-
 3. Pain and Suffering 50,000/-
 4. Loss of amenities 30,000/-
 5. Transportation, extra 30,000/-

sentences.text:
In the result, the following order is passed:
 (i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The claimant is entitled for the total compensation of Rs.6,88,671/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.

(iii) The respondent insurance company has already deposited the award amount before the Tribunal, and therefore, they are directed to deposit the enhanced amount of Rs.1,16,948/- with interest at 6% per annum within one month from the date of this order.
(iv) On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with the interest accrued on it.
NC: 2026:KHC:6910 HC-KAR
(v) In view of the order dated 07.11.2025 passed on I.A.No.1/2025, the claimant is not entitled for interest for the delayed period of 221 days in filing the appeal.
(vi) Learned counsel for respondent No.2 is permitted to file vakalath within two weeks.

Sd/-
